answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not try to add the two missed runs on top of three new ones. Missed sessions during illness are gone, not owed; piling them in now is the fastest route to another setback. Three runs this week, starting shorter than last week's plan, is the right move. If Monday feels clean and the cough is fading, Wednesday and Saturday grow back toward where you were.

new.analysis:
## What happened and why it matters

You got one run in on Mon Sep 7 before the cold hit, then the fever on Wed night sensibly ended the week. That is the right call, not a failure. The Monday run itself was solid: steady pace, heart rate drift basically flat, pain 0/10.

## How we come back

Build phase on paper, but your real build is still "run longer between walk breaks." We rebuild from a slightly easier start than last week's Monday, because you are two days past a fever and still coughing. The first run tells us how much of the week is on.

## Rule for this week

If the cough gets worse during a run, or you feel chest tightness, breathlessness beyond effort, or dizziness, stop and rest the next day. Dial back the Saturday session to the Wednesday shape if you are not clearly better by Friday. We would rather land in Nov 15 slightly undercooked than miss another week.

safetyCallouts.title: Returning to running after a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: You had 38.4 on Wed and are still coughing. If the cough worsens with exercise, if you feel chest pain or tightness, unusual breathlessness, a racing heart at rest, or dizziness, stop running and see your GP before the next session. Build back gradually this week rather than chasing the missed runs.
